title: Compatibility-first intake lane for customer-sensitive models with audit-linked eval gates
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are requesting a dedicated intake flow for models that must meet strict compatibility and audit traceability requirements (e.g., regulated PII processing, internal embeddings compatibility). Current catalog intake treats all submissions uniformly which increases review friction, slows enterprise onboarding, and risks inadvertent regressions when models are pinned or deprecated.

Proposal: Create a new 'compatibility-first' intake lane in the model catalog UI and triage process that routes customer-sensitive submissions through a structured, audit-linked eval path. This lane includes: (1) mandatory compatibility checklist metadata at intake (schema, tokenizer, default temperature ranges, expected latency), (2) a reproducible eval sampling policy that stores seed prompts and deterministic eval output in the audit log, (3) a contractual pinning SLA template and suggested deprecation windows, and (4) an emergency pin/rollback playbook tied to Dedicated/Private routing. The lane should be surfaced in the intake form, available via API, and produce a per-submission audit artifact (eval snapshot + reviewer decisions) that can be exported to compliance teams.

Why unique: Unlike general-purpose intake playbooks, this lane prioritizes deterministic reproducibility, auditability, and fast recovery. It is designed for customers who require deterministic behavior across model variants or need to prove behavior for a regulated workload.

Scope: UI intake changes, backend routing rules, eval harness extension (snapshot storage + immutable tags), addition of a 'contractual pin' recommendation generator, and runbook for emergency pin/rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Intake UI has a selectable 'compatibility-first' lane with required metadata fields (schema, tokenizer, expected latencies, business-critical prompts)
API intake supports a compatibility flag and accepts the required metadata programmatically
Eval harness can run deterministic sample sets, persist outputs as immutable audit artifacts, and link artifact IDs to the catalog entry
Reviewer workflow surfaces audit artifacts and includes explicit decisions (approve/pin/decline) and a rationale field
Contractual pinning SLA template is draft-ready and available to customer success for 1:1 negotiation
Emergency pin/rollback playbook validated in a tabletop run and documented in Console runbooks
decisions: Use a lightweight seed-prompt set (50 prompts) for initial deterministic sampling; allow expansion per customer needs
Persist eval artifacts in append-only storage with stable identifiers that tie to model version and intake ID
Recommend default pin duration of 90 days for enterprise-critical models with option for negotiated extensions
Route compatibility-first traffic to Dedicated or Private by default; allow Hosted only with explicit customer waiver
open_questions: What storage SLA and retention policy for eval artifacts satisfies both compliance and cost constraints?
How do we represent tokenizer/schema compatibility metadata across different model families (transformers, quantized variants)?
Should emergency pinning automatically redirect traffic to the last-approved variant or to a read-only mode?
Do we need an additional UI permission role for 'Compliance Reviewer' separate from Product/Eng reviewers?
tasks: Design intake UI fields and copy (DX/Design)
Implement deterministic eval sampling and immutable artifact storage (Evals team)
Add review UI affordances and audit export (Console team)
Draft contractual pin SLA template and legal review (PM/Legal)
Create emergency pin/rollback runbook and test in staging (SRE/Runbooks)
progress_updates: 2026-03-14: Drafted proposal and acceptance criteria. Aligned with Legal for SLA template prerequisites. Identified Evals and Console owners. Submitted to intake roadmap sync.
metrics: Time-to-approve for compatibility-first submissions (target: <= 10 business days)
Number of emergency pins invoked per quarter (target: 0-2)
Fraction of enterprise onboarding that uses compatibility-first lane (target: >= 40% within 6 months)
Audit artifact retrieval latency (target: < 2s for console queries)
